newsitem.title: UK: UK services show strong growth in April-CIPS.
newsitem.headline: UK services show strong growth in April-CIPS.

text.p: Britain's service sector continued to show strong growth in April, with new business, employment, prices charged and input prices all increasing, the Chartered Institute of Purchasing and Supply (CIPS) said.

Its business activity index, based on information from 500 executives in private sector industries, dipped to a seasonally adjusted 61.2 from 63.3 in March but this reflected sharply rising demand for services. An index reading above 50 indicates growth. "Almost a third of all companies surveyed reported a rise in business activity while less than 10 percent reported a decline," the CIPS said.
Its services survey, the sister index of the purchasing managers' survey of manufacturing, is sponsored by Reuters.
Employment showed a further significant increase as companies raised capacity to meet further strong growth of incoming new business.
"However, the amount of business outstanding rose again, suggesting that firms have yet to raise capacity sufficiently to fully meet the growth of demand for services," the CIPS said.
A shortage of skilled personnel limited companies' scope to boost capacity, especially in information technology.
"The shortage of suitable labour was reflected in a rise in wages and salaries," the CIPS said.
"Average input prices, of which salaries tend to form the lion's share in the service sector, showed the largest monthly rise since the survey began."

The seasonally adjusted incoming new business index was 62.1 compared with 62.4, a rise similar to that seen the previous month, despite reports that uncertainty due to the election had caused a temporary slowdown in some sectors, especially financial services.
The outstanding business index was 53.5 against 57.7 in March, singalling a further increase in work in hand.
The employment index was 55.4 in April against 57.6 the previous month, reflecting a further increase in recruitment.
"Over a fifth of all firms took on additional staff in April to meet rising levels of business activity -- more than double the number of firms that cut staff during the month," the CIPS said.
Average prices charged rose for the sixth consecutive month, with an index reading of 52.2 compared with 51.6 in March.
"However, the total number of companies able to raise their charges continued to be subdued by strong competitive pressures."
Average input prices rose to 57.9 from 57.0, the largest rise since the survey began, reflecting a sharp increase in costs in April, due principally to rising salaries.
The business expectations index dropped modestly for the third month running but remained very strong, with an index reading of 83.0 against 84.6 in March.
